questions.questionText: Which sound does a cow make?
questions.explanation: A cow says moo.

questions.questionText: A dog says ___. What is the sound?
questions.explanation: A dog barks, so it says woof.

questions.questionText: What sound does a cat make?
questions.explanation: A cat says meow.

questions.questionText: Which sound comes from a duck?
questions.explanation: A duck says quack.

questions.questionText: A bird makes which sound?
questions.explanation: A bird chirps.

questions.questionText: What noise does a snake make?
questions.explanation: A snake hisses.

questions.questionText: A pig says ___. What is it?
questions.explanation: A pig says oink.

questions.questionText: Which sound does a bee make?
questions.explanation: A bee buzzes.

questions.questionText: Your teacher says the /b/ sound. Which word starts with it?
questions.explanation: Ball starts with /b/.

questions.questionText: Which word begins with the /k/ sound?
questions.explanation: Kite begins with /k/.

questions.questionText: Find the word that starts with the /m/ sound.
questions.explanation: Milk starts with /m/.

questions.questionText: The /s/ sound is at the beginning of which word?
questions.explanation: Sun begins with /s/.

questions.questionText: Which word has the first sound /t/?
questions.explanation: Tiger starts with /t/.

questions.questionText: Which word starts with a /d/ sound?
questions.explanation: Dog begins with /d/.

questions.questionText: Pick the word that begins with /p/.
questions.explanation: Pen starts with /p/.

questions.questionText: The sound /h/ is the first sound in which word?
questions.explanation: Hat begins with /h/.

questions.questionText: Which word begins with the /f/ sound?
questions.explanation: Fish starts with /f/.

questions.questionText: Which word rhymes with 'cat'?
questions.explanation: Cat and hat rhyme.

questions.questionText: Find the word that rhymes with 'dog'.
questions.explanation: Dog and frog rhyme.

questions.questionText: Which word sounds the same at the end as 'run'?
questions.explanation: Run and sun rhyme.

questions.questionText: 'bed' rhymes with which word?
questions.explanation: Bed and red rhyme.

questions.questionText: The teacher says 'moon'. Which word starts with the same sound?
questions.explanation: Moon and monkey both start with /m/.

questions.questionText: The teacher says 'fish'. Which word starts with the same sound?
questions.explanation: Fish and fan both start with /f/.

questions.questionText: Which word ends with the /t/ sound?
questions.explanation: Cat ends with /t/.

questions.questionText: Which word has the same middle vowel sound as 'cat'?
questions.explanation: Cat and hat have the same middle vowel.

questions.questionText: It is yellow and long. Monkeys love to eat it. What is it?
questions.explanation: A banana is yellow and monkeys eat it.

questions.questionText: This animal says 'woof' and wags its tail. What is it?
questions.explanation: A dog says woof.

questions.questionText: It is a colour. The sky and the sea are this colour.
questions.explanation: The sky and sea are blue.

questions.questionText: Which number is one more than three?
questions.explanation: One more than three is four.

questions.questionText: You write with it. It is long and thin with a point.
questions.explanation: A pencil is long, thin and has a point.

questions.questionText: Your mother's mother is your ___.
questions.explanation: Mother's mother is grandmother.

questions.questionText: It is on your face and you see with it.
questions.explanation: You see with your eye.

questions.questionText: This big animal has a long nose called a trunk.
questions.explanation: An elephant has a trunk.

questions.questionText: It is red and round. Snow White ate one.
questions.explanation: An apple is red and round.

questions.questionText: You sit on it in class. It has four legs.
questions.explanation: You sit on a chair.

questions.questionText: It is a colour. Grass and leaves are this colour.
questions.explanation: Grass and leaves are green.

questions.questionText: Your father's son is your ___.
questions.explanation: Father's son is your brother.

questions.questionText: It is cold and sweet. You eat it in summer, usually in a cone.
questions.explanation: Ice cream is cold and comes in a cone.

questions.questionText: It is in the kitchen and it bakes bread.
questions.explanation: An oven bakes bread.

questions.questionText: It is a number. It comes after nine.
questions.explanation: Ten comes after nine.

questions.questionText: You wear these on your feet when you go out.
questions.explanation: You wear shoes on your feet.

questions.questionText: It flies in the sky and sings sweet songs.
questions.explanation: A bird flies and sings.

questions.questionText: It lives in water, has fins and a tail, but cannot walk.
questions.explanation: A fish lives in water.

questions.questionText: Your uncle's son is your ___.
questions.explanation: Uncle's son is your cousin.

questions.questionText: It is a colour. The sun and a lemon are this colour.
questions.explanation: The sun and a lemon are yellow.

questions.questionText: You open it to enter the classroom.
questions.explanation: You open the door to enter.

questions.questionText: It has many pages and you read it in class.
questions.explanation: A book has pages.

questions.questionText: They are on your hands and you have ten of them.
questions.explanation: You have ten fingers.

questions.questionText: It is white and cold, and falls from the sky in winter.
questions.explanation: Snow is white and cold.

questions.questionText: You use it to clean the board. It is near the board.
questions.explanation: A duster cleans the board.

questions.questionText: It is a family word. Your aunt's husband is your ___.
questions.explanation: Aunt's husband is uncle.

questions.questionText: It is a number. Two and two make ___.
questions.explanation: Two and two make four.

questions.questionText: It is round. You kick it on the field with your feet.
questions.explanation: You kick a ball.

questions.questionText: You smell with it. It is on your face.
questions.explanation: You smell with your nose.

questions.questionText: It goes 'tick tock' and wakes you up in the morning.
questions.explanation: A clock goes tick tock.

questions.questionText: Your teacher says, 'Open your book.' What do you do?
questions.explanation: 'Open your book' means open your book.

questions.questionText: The teacher says, 'Stand up.' What do you do?
questions.explanation: 'Stand up' means rise from your seat.

questions.questionText: 'Sit down, please.' What does the teacher want you to do?
questions.explanation: 'Sit down' means take your seat.

questions.questionText: 'Be quiet, children.' What does the teacher want?
questions.explanation: 'Be quiet' means do not make noise.

questions.questionText: The teacher says, 'Touch your nose.' What do you touch?
questions.explanation: The instruction names the nose.

questions.questionText: 'Clap your hands.' What do you do?
questions.explanation: Clap means hit your hands together.

questions.questionText: 'Look at the board.' Where do you look?
questions.explanation: The instruction tells you to look at the board.

questions.questionText: 'Pick up your pencil.' What do you pick up?
questions.explanation: The instruction names the pencil.

questions.questionText: The teacher says, 'Colour the apple red.' What colour do you use?
questions.explanation: The instruction says to use red.

questions.questionText: 'Line up at the door.' Where do you go?
questions.explanation: Line up at the door.

questions.questionText: 'Close the window, please.' What do you close?
questions.explanation: The instruction names the window.

questions.questionText: 'Give me your rubber.' What does the teacher want?
questions.explanation: 'Give me your rubber' asks for the rubber.

questions.questionText: 'Show me your picture.' What do you show?
questions.explanation: The instruction asks for the picture.

questions.questionText: Your teacher asks, 'What is your name?' What does she want to know?
questions.explanation: The question asks for your name.

questions.questionText: 'How old are you?' What does the question ask?
questions.explanation: 'How old' asks about age.

questions.questionText: Your teacher asks, 'Is it raining today?' What does she want to know?
questions.explanation: 'Is it raining' asks about the weather.

questions.questionText: 'Where is your bag?' What does the teacher want to know?
questions.explanation: 'Where' asks about place.

questions.questionText: The teacher says, 'Take out your book and open it to page one.' What do you do first?
questions.explanation: The first step is to take out your book.

questions.questionText: 'Stand up, walk to the door, and open it.' What do you do second?
questions.explanation: The middle step is walking to the door.

questions.questionText: 'Put your pencil in the box.' Where does your pencil go?
questions.explanation: The instruction says in the box.

questions.questionText: Your friend says, 'I have a red car.' What colour is the car?
questions.explanation: The sentence says the car is red.

questions.questionText: 'Lily has two cats.' How many cats does Lily have?
questions.explanation: The sentence says two cats.

questions.questionText: 'The boy with the blue bag is my brother.' Who has the blue bag?
questions.explanation: The boy with the blue bag is my brother.

questions.questionText: 'Give the book to Sara.' Who gets the book?
questions.explanation: The instruction says give it to Sara.

questions.questionText: 'Listen to me, please.' What does the teacher want?
questions.explanation: 'Listen to me' means pay attention.

questions.questionText: 'Don't run in the classroom.' What must you not do?
questions.explanation: 'Don't run' forbids running.

questions.questionText: 'Touch your ears, then close your eyes.' What do you do after touching your ears?
questions.explanation: After touching ears, close your eyes.

questions.questionText: 'What is this?' It is a picture of a dog. What do you answer?
questions.explanation: The picture shows a dog.

questions.questionText: 'Is your father a teacher?' Your father is a doctor. What do you say?
questions.explanation: Your father is a doctor, so answer no.

questions.questionText: 'How many pencils do you have?' You have three. What do you say?
questions.explanation: Answer the number, three.

questions.questionText: 'Good morning, teacher.' When do you say this?
questions.explanation: Good morning is said in the morning.

questions.questionText: 'Please pass me the salt.' What does the speaker want?
questions.explanation: The request asks for the salt.

questions.questionText: 'The baby is sleeping.' What must you be?
questions.explanation: A sleeping baby means you must be quiet.

questions.questionText: 'Put the apple on the plate, not on the floor.' Where does the apple go?
questions.explanation: The instruction says on the plate.

questions.questionText: 'Which animal says moo?' What is the answer?
questions.explanation: A cow says moo.

questions.questionText: I ___ a pupil.
questions.explanation: We use am after I.

questions.questionText: She ___ my mother.
questions.explanation: We use is with she.

questions.questionText: They ___ my friends.
questions.explanation: We use are with they.

questions.questionText: This is ___ apple.
questions.explanation: Apple starts with a vowel sound, so use an.

questions.questionText: That is ___ ball.
questions.explanation: Ball starts with a consonant, so use a.

questions.questionText: ___ is my brother. He is tall.
questions.explanation: Brother is male, so use He.

questions.questionText: This is my sister. ___ is six years old.
questions.explanation: Sister is female, so use She.

questions.questionText: I have two ___.
questions.explanation: Two needs the plural pens.

questions.questionText: My father and mother ___ at home.
questions.explanation: Two people is plural, so we use 'are'.

questions.questionText: ___ name is Tom.
questions.explanation: Use my before a name.

questions.questionText: What is ___ name?
questions.explanation: Use your before name.

questions.questionText: The dog ___ brown.
questions.explanation: The dog is one animal, so we use is.

questions.questionText: We ___ in Class One.
questions.explanation: We use are with we.

questions.questionText: There ___ three books on the desk.
questions.explanation: Three books is plural, so are.

questions.questionText: ___ you fine today?
questions.explanation: We use are with you.

questions.questionText: This is ___ umbrella.
questions.explanation: Umbrella starts with a vowel sound, so an.

questions.questionText: The ___ are playing in the garden.
questions.explanation: Are needs the plural children.

questions.questionText: I have ___ egg for breakfast.
questions.explanation: Egg starts with a vowel sound, so an.

questions.questionText: Those ___ my shoes.
questions.explanation: We use are with those.

questions.questionText: ___ is my teacher, Ms Lee.
questions.explanation: Use This to introduce one person.

questions.questionText: My cat ___ white.
questions.explanation: My cat is one animal, so we use is.

questions.questionText: I have three ___.
questions.explanation: Plural of box is boxes.

questions.questionText: ___ am a boy.
questions.explanation: Am goes with I.

questions.questionText: You ___ my good friend.
questions.explanation: We use are with you.

questions.questionText: It is ___ orange on the table.
questions.explanation: Orange starts with a vowel sound, so an.

questions.questionText: Good ___!
questions.explanation: Good morning is a greeting.

questions.questionText: How ___ you?
questions.explanation: How are you?

questions.questionText: Nice to ___ you.
questions.explanation: Nice to meet you.

questions.questionText: Thank ___.
questions.explanation: Thank you.

questions.questionText: Goodbye! See you ___.
questions.explanation: See you tomorrow.

questions.questionText: What is your ___?
questions.explanation: The question asks for your name.

questions.questionText: I am eight ___ old.
questions.explanation: Eight years old.

questions.questionText: This is ___ friend, Ahmad.
questions.explanation: Use my before friend.

questions.questionText: Sit ___, please.
questions.explanation: Sit down, please.

questions.questionText: Please ___ the door.
questions.explanation: Please + base verb open.

questions.questionText: —How are you? —I'm ___, thank you.
questions.explanation: I'm fine, thank you.

questions.questionText: Hello! My ___ is Tom.
questions.explanation: My name is Tom.

questions.questionText: Good ___! It is nine o'clock at night.
questions.explanation: At night we say good night.

questions.questionText: ___ you are.
questions.explanation: Here you are.

questions.questionText: —Thank you very much. —You're ___.
questions.explanation: Reply to thanks with You're welcome.

questions.questionText: Please ___ the window. It is hot in here.
questions.explanation: It is hot, so open the window.

questions.questionText: Stand ___, please.
questions.explanation: Stand up, please.

questions.questionText: I have a ___. I write with it.
questions.explanation: You write with a pencil.

questions.questionText: —How old are you? —___ nine.
questions.explanation: I am nine.

questions.questionText: This is my ___. She is my mother's mother.
questions.explanation: Mother's mother is grandmother.

questions.questionText: Look ___ the board.
questions.explanation: Look at the board.

questions.questionText: —Goodbye, see you tomorrow. —___
questions.explanation: Reply to goodbye with Bye.

questions.questionText: I ___ a red apple.
questions.explanation: I have a red apple.

questions.questionText: It ___ a cat.
questions.explanation: We use is with it.

questions.questionText: —What is your name? —___ name is Anna.
questions.explanation: My name is Anna.

questions.questionText: The book is ___ the table.
questions.explanation: The book is on the table.

questions.questionText: Colour the apple ___.
questions.explanation: We put a colour word such as red here.

questions.questionText: I can ___ a bird in the sky.
questions.explanation: Can + base verb see.

questions.questionText: —Nice to meet you. —Nice to meet you ___.
questions.explanation: Reply with too (also).

questions.questionText: ___ is my bag? It is on the chair.
questions.explanation: Where asks about place.

questions.questionText: Pick the correct sentence.
questions.explanation: Correct order is I am a pupil.

questions.questionText: Tick the right sentence.
questions.explanation: We introduce with This is my mother.

questions.questionText: Which of these is correct?
questions.explanation: Correct order is I like apples.

questions.questionText: Find the correct sentence.
questions.explanation: Correct word order.

questions.questionText: Which line of English is right?

options.label: C
options.text: The cat is on the mat.

questions.explanation: Correct order.

questions.questionText: Choose the sentence that is correct.
questions.explanation: Correct order.

questions.questionText: Which sentence asks for your name?
questions.explanation: Correct question order.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct greeting.
questions.explanation: We say Good morning, teacher!

questions.questionText: Which sentence is written correctly?
questions.explanation: Correct order.

questions.questionText: Which sentence says thank you for a gift?
questions.explanation: Correct order.

questions.questionText: Only one sentence is correct. Which one?
questions.explanation: Correct order.

questions.questionText: Which sentence is proper English?
questions.explanation: Correct polite instruction.

questions.questionText: Which sentence introduces yourself?

options.label: D
options.text: I am Tom. I am seven.

questions.explanation: Correct self-introduction.

questions.questionText: Pick the sentence with the right word order.
questions.explanation: Correct order.

questions.questionText: Which sentence is correct?
questions.explanation: Correct question order.

questions.questionText: Which is a correct reply to 'Thank you'?
questions.explanation: Correct fixed reply.

questions.questionText: Which sentence has the right word order?

options.label: B
options.text: Go we to school bus by.

options.label: C
options.text: We by bus go to school.

options.label: D
options.text: We go to school by bus.

questions.explanation: Correct order.

questions.questionText: Which sentence is right?
questions.explanation: A plural subject like the boys goes with are.

questions.questionText: Choose the well-written sentence.
questions.explanation: Correct order.

questions.questionText: Which sentence is correct here?
questions.explanation: Correct order.

questions.questionText: You meet your teacher at school in the morning. You say: ___.
questions.explanation: Morning meeting needs Good morning.

questions.questionText: A classmate gives you a pencil. You say: ___.
questions.explanation: When given something, say Thank you.

questions.questionText: School is over and you leave the classroom. You say: ___.
questions.explanation: When leaving, say Goodbye.

questions.questionText: You want your friend to pass you the book. You say politely: ___.
questions.explanation: Use please to be polite.

questions.questionText: You do not hear your teacher. What do you say?
questions.explanation: Ask Pardon? to repeat.

questions.questionText: You step on your friend's foot by accident. You say: ___.
questions.explanation: For a small mistake, say Sorry.

questions.questionText: Someone says 'Thank you' to you. What do you say in return?
questions.explanation: Reply to thanks with You're welcome.

questions.questionText: You meet a new friend. What do you say?
questions.explanation: Greet and give your name.

questions.questionText: Your friend asks, 'How are you?' What do you say?
questions.explanation: Answer how you feel.

questions.questionText: You want to ask the teacher a question. What do you say first?
questions.explanation: Get attention politely with Excuse me.

questions.questionText: It is twelve o'clock and you meet your friend. You say: ___.
questions.explanation: Midday greeting is Good afternoon.

questions.questionText: Your friend says, ‘Well done! You read very well!’ after your turn in class. What do you say?
questions.explanation: When a friend praises you, you say thank you.

questions.questionText: You are cold and want the window closed. You say: ___.
questions.explanation: Ask politely to close it.

questions.questionText: You do not understand a word in class. What do you say?
questions.explanation: Ask the teacher to repeat.

questions.questionText: Your friend says, 'Goodbye!' What do you say?
questions.explanation: Reply warmly to goodbye.

questions.questionText: Which small letter matches the capital letter ‘B’?
questions.explanation: The small letter of B is b. It has the tall stick and the round belly on the same side.

questions.questionText: What is the capital letter for the small letter ‘r’?
questions.explanation: Small r pairs with capital R.

questions.questionText: Which small letter has the same shape as the capital ‘G’?
questions.explanation: Capital G and small g share the same round shape with a tail.

questions.questionText: Which capital letter matches the small letter ‘w’?
questions.explanation: Small w is the twin shape of capital W.

questions.questionText: What is the small letter for the capital ‘Y’?
questions.explanation: Capital Y goes with small y.

questions.questionText: Which letter comes between ‘L’ and ‘N’ in the alphabet?
questions.explanation: The alphabet order is L, M, N.

questions.questionText: The capital ‘E’ has three lines. Which small letter is its pair?
questions.explanation: Capital E pairs with small e.

questions.questionText: Which small letter looks exactly like the tall capital ‘M’ but short?
questions.explanation: Small m has the same two bumps as capital M.

questions.questionText: Which two letters look most alike in shape?
questions.explanation: b and d are mirror images of each other and are easily mixed up.

questions.questionText: Point to the small letter ‘p’?
questions.explanation: p has a round belly on the right and a tail hanging down on the left.

questions.questionText: Which small letter has its tail hanging down on the right side?
questions.explanation: q is a circle with a tail going down on the right.

questions.questionText: Which choice shows the small letter ‘q’?
questions.explanation: q has a round belly and a tail down; g and y have different tails.

questions.questionText: What is the first sound in the word ‘book’?
questions.explanation: book starts with the sound /b/.

questions.questionText: Which word begins with the same sound as ‘sun’?
questions.explanation: sun /s/ and sat /s/ start with the same sound.

questions.questionText: The word ‘fish’ begins with which sound?
questions.explanation: fish begins with /f/, made by the letter f.

questions.questionText: Find the word that begins with /m/.
questions.explanation: mat begins with /m/.

questions.questionText: What is the beginning sound in ‘red’?
questions.explanation: red starts with /r/.

questions.questionText: Find the word that starts like ‘pen’?
questions.explanation: pen /p/ and pig /p/ share the same opening sound.

questions.questionText: The word ‘van’ begins with which letter?
questions.explanation: van starts with the letter v making /v/; /v/ and /w/ sound very close.

questions.questionText: Which word has the opening sound /h/?
questions.explanation: hat begins with /h/.

questions.questionText: What is the first sound in ‘dog’?
questions.explanation: dog starts with /d/; /d/, /t/ and /b/ are close sounds that are easily mixed up.

questions.questionText: The word that starts with /k/ is ___.
questions.explanation: cup starts with the letter c making /k/.

questions.questionText: The first sound in ‘web’ is ___.
questions.explanation: web begins with /w/.

questions.questionText: The opening sound of ‘hat’ matches which word?
questions.explanation: hat /h/ and hen /h/ start the same way.

questions.questionText: What letter does ‘jam’ start with?
questions.explanation: jam starts with the letter j.

questions.questionText: Pick the word which begins with /s/.
questions.explanation: sit begins with /s/.

questions.questionText: The first sound of ‘box’ is ___.
questions.explanation: box starts with /b/.

questions.questionText: Which word shares the first sound with ‘map’?
questions.explanation: map /m/ and man /m/ share the first sound; pan /p/ sounds very close to /m/.

questions.questionText: What is the last sound in ‘hat’?
questions.explanation: hat ends with the sound /t/.

questions.questionText: Which word has the ending sound /p/?
questions.explanation: cup ends with /p/.

questions.questionText: The last sound of ‘bed’ is ___.
questions.explanation: bed ends with /d/.

questions.questionText: Which word ends with the same sound as ‘pig’?
questions.explanation: pig ends with /g/, and dog also ends with /g/.

questions.questionText: What is the ending sound in ‘bus’?
questions.explanation: bus ends with /s/.

questions.questionText: The word that ends with /t/ is ___.
questions.explanation: net ends with /t/; /t/ and /n/ are close final sounds.

questions.questionText: The last sound of ‘cap’ is ___.
questions.explanation: cap ends with /p/.

questions.questionText: Which word closes with the same final sound as ‘pen’?
questions.explanation: pen ends in /n/, and hen also ends in /n/.

questions.questionText: What is the final sound in ‘milk’?
questions.explanation: milk ends with the sound /k/.

questions.questionText: Pick the word which closes with /n/.
questions.explanation: van ends with /n/; /n/ and /t/ sound close at the end of a word.

questions.questionText: The last sound of ‘rug’ is ___.
questions.explanation: rug ends with /g/.

questions.questionText: The ending of ‘red’ matches which word?
questions.explanation: red ends in /d/, and bed also ends in /d/.

questions.questionText: What is the final sound in ‘mop’?
questions.explanation: mop ends with /p/.

questions.questionText: What is the middle sound in ‘hat’?
questions.explanation: hat has the middle vowel sound /a/.

questions.questionText: Which word has the same middle sound as ‘pen’?
questions.explanation: pen /e/ and bed /e/ share the middle vowel.

questions.questionText: What is the middle sound in ‘pig’?
questions.explanation: pig has the middle sound /i/; telling middle vowels apart is the tricky part.

questions.questionText: Find the word with the same vowel sound as ‘dog’?
questions.explanation: dog and pot both have the middle vowel /o/.

questions.questionText: The middle sound of ‘cup’ is ___.
questions.explanation: cup has the middle vowel /u/.

questions.questionText: Which word shares the middle sound with ‘mat’?
questions.explanation: mat and bag share the middle vowel /a/.

questions.questionText: What is the middle sound in ‘red’?
questions.explanation: red has the middle vowel /e/.

questions.questionText: Find the word whose middle vowel matches ‘sit’?
questions.explanation: sit and fin share the middle vowel /i/.

questions.questionText: The middle sound of ‘hot’ is ___.
questions.explanation: hot has the middle vowel /o/.

questions.questionText: Which word has the /a/ middle sound?
questions.explanation: cat has the middle vowel /a/.

questions.questionText: The middle sound of ‘hen’ matches which word?
questions.explanation: hen and pen share /e/; pan, pin and bun have other middle vowels.

questions.questionText: Pick the word with the same middle vowel as ‘map’?
questions.explanation: map and cap share the middle vowel /a/.

questions.questionText: Blend the sounds /c/ /a/ /t/. What word is it?
questions.explanation: Blending /c/+/a/+/t/ gives cat.

questions.questionText: What word do these sounds make? /s/ /i/ /t/
questions.explanation: /s/+/i/+/t/ blends into sit.

questions.questionText: The sounds /d/ /o/ /g/ blend into ___.
questions.explanation: /d/+/o/+/g/ makes dog.

questions.questionText: Which sounds blend to make the word ‘pen’?
questions.explanation: pen is made of the sounds p, e, n.

questions.questionText: Blend /h/ /a/ /t/. What is the word?
questions.explanation: /h/+/a/+/t/ makes hat.

questions.questionText: What word do /m/ /u/ /g/ make?
questions.explanation: /m/+/u/+/g/ blends into mug.

questions.questionText: Which sounds blend to make the word ‘bus’?
questions.explanation: bus is made of b, u, s.

questions.questionText: What word do the sounds /f/ /i/ /n/ make?
questions.explanation: /f/+/i/+/n/ blends into fin.

questions.questionText: Which sounds blend to make the word ‘red’?
questions.explanation: red is made of the sounds r, e, d.

questions.questionText: Say these sounds together: /s/ /t/ /o/ /p/. Which word do they make?
questions.explanation: /s/+/t/+/o/+/p/ blends into stop; spot starts with /sp/, not /st/.

questions.questionText: How many sounds are in the word ‘flag’?
questions.explanation: flag splits into four sounds: /f/, /l/, /a/, /g/.

questions.questionText: Which word begins with the two sounds /f/ /l/?
questions.explanation: flag starts with /fl/; frog starts with /fr/.

questions.questionText: I have ___ umbrella in my bag.
questions.explanation: umbrella starts with a vowel sound, so we use an.

questions.questionText: The dog ___ a short tail.
questions.explanation: We use has with the dog (it).

questions.questionText: We write words with a ___ .
questions.explanation: We write with a pencil.

questions.questionText: My sister is ___ the bedroom.
questions.explanation: inside a room uses in.

questions.questionText: Good morning, Miss Lee. ___ to see you.
questions.explanation: The fixed phrase is 'Nice to see you.'

questions.questionText: The dog is sleeping ___ the table.
questions.explanation: below the table uses under.

questions.questionText: I have two ___ .
questions.explanation: two apples: add -s to make the plural.

questions.questionText: ___ is that boy? He is my brother.
questions.explanation: Asking about a person uses Who.

questions.questionText: There ___ forty pupils in our class.
questions.explanation: We use are with forty pupils (plural).

questions.questionText: The children ___ playing in the field now.
questions.explanation: We use are with the children (plural, now).

questions.questionText: My grandfather ___ fishing at the weekend.
questions.explanation: We use goes with My grandfather (he).

questions.questionText: Please pass me ___ ruler on the desk.
questions.explanation: the ruler on the desk is a specific ruler, so use the.

questions.questionText: We have Art ___ Tuesday.
questions.explanation: days of the week use on.

questions.questionText: The baby is sleeping. Please ___ quiet.
questions.explanation: imperative: Please be quiet.

questions.questionText: ___ your name, please?
questions.explanation: Asking about a name uses What is your name?

questions.questionText: I am thirsty. Please give me a glass of ___ .
questions.explanation: thirsty means we want a drink, water.

questions.questionText: The box of crayons ___ on the table.
questions.explanation: The subject The box is singular, so we use is.

questions.questionText: There isn't ___ milk left in the glass.
questions.explanation: In a negative sentence we use any milk.

questions.questionText: Look at those ___ over there.
questions.explanation: The plural of child is children (irregular).

questions.questionText: Which sentence begins with a capital letter?
questions.explanation: The first word of a sentence starts with a capital letter; the other words are small letters.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct sentence.
questions.explanation: Subject I + have + a red bag.

questions.questionText: Which is a correct sentence?

options.label: A
options.text: The sun rise in the east.

options.label: B
options.text: The sun are in the east rises.

options.label: C
options.text: The sun rising in the east.

options.label: D
options.text: The sun rises in the east.

questions.explanation: We use rises with The sun (it).

questions.questionText: Pick the sentence with the correct punctuation.
questions.explanation: A question starts with a capital letter and ends with a question mark.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct pronoun: ___ is my mother.
questions.explanation: mother is a woman, so we use She.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct plural: one cat - two ___
questions.explanation: Add -s: cat - cats.

questions.questionText: Which sentence uses the verb with 'they' correctly?

options.label: A
options.text: They are playing football in the field.

options.label: B
options.text: They playing are football in field.

options.label: C
options.text: They are play football in the field.

options.label: D
options.text: They is playing football in the field.

questions.explanation: We use are playing with They (plural).

questions.questionText: Which sentence uses the right verb for 'my brother'?

options.label: A
options.text: My brother goes to school by a bus.

options.label: B
options.text: My brother go to school by bus.

options.label: C
options.text: My brother going to school by bus.

options.label: D
options.text: My brother goes to school by bus.

questions.explanation: We use goes with My brother (he); by bus has no article.

questions.questionText: Which sentence uses 'and' correctly?

options.label: A
options.text: I have a pen or a pencil and.

options.label: B
options.text: And I have a pen a pencil.

options.label: C
options.text: I have a pen and a pencil.

options.label: D
options.text: I have a pen but a pencil.

questions.explanation: and joins two nouns in one list.

questions.questionText: Which sentence about 'the children' is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: The childrens are in the playground.

options.label: B
options.text: The childs are in the playground.

options.label: C
options.text: The children is in the playground.

options.label: D
options.text: The children are in the playground.

questions.explanation: children is already plural, so we use are.

questions.questionText: Which sentence has the correct capital letters?

options.label: A
options.text: My aunt lives in kuala lumpur.

options.label: B
options.text: My Aunt Lives In Kuala Lumpur.

options.label: C
options.text: My aunt lives in Kuala Lumpur.

options.label: D
options.text: My aunt lives in Kuala lumpur.

questions.explanation: Place names start with capital letters: Kuala Lumpur.

questions.questionText: Which sentence about the water in the bottle is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: There are some water in the bottle.

options.label: B
options.text: There is some waters in the bottle.

options.label: C
options.text: There is a water in the bottle.

options.label: D
options.text: There is some water in the bottle.

questions.explanation: water is uncountable, so we use is.

questions.questionText: Which sentence uses the right verb for 'my friends'?

options.label: A
options.text: My friends plays football every evening.

options.label: B
options.text: My friends playing football every evening.

options.label: C
options.text: My friends play football every evening.

options.label: D
options.text: My friends playes football every evening.

questions.explanation: We use play with My friends (plural).

questions.questionText: Which sentence uses the correct verb with 'the boy'?

options.label: A
options.text: The boy with the blue cap are my cousin.

options.label: B
options.text: The boy with the blue cap be my cousin.

options.label: C
options.text: The boy with the blue cap is my cousin.

options.label: D
options.text: The boy with the blue cap am my cousin.

questions.explanation: The subject The boy is singular, so we use is; with the blue cap is extra information.

questions.questionText: Which sentence uses the plural nouns correctly?

options.label: A
options.text: I have two foots and ten toes.

options.label: B
options.text: I have two feet and ten toes's.

options.label: C
options.text: I have two feet and ten toes.

options.label: D
options.text: I have two foot and ten toe.

questions.explanation: Irregular plurals: foot - feet; toe - toes.

questions.questionText: In an action song, when the teacher says 'Clap your hands', we ___ .
questions.explanation: clap means to hit our hands together.

questions.questionText: What do we do when we 'stamp our feet'?

options.label: A
options.text: turn our body all the way around

options.label: B
options.text: nod our head up and down

options.label: C
options.text: wave our hands from side to side

options.label: D
options.text: bring our feet down hard on the floor

questions.explanation: stamp means to bring a foot down hard.

questions.questionText: Which word is an action word?
questions.explanation: jump tells us to do something; the others are nouns or colours.

questions.questionText: When the teacher says 'Wave your hand', we ___ .

options.label: A
options.text: hold the pencil with three fingers

options.label: B
options.text: close the book on the desk

options.label: C
options.text: move our hand from side to side

options.label: D
options.text: sit down quietly on the chair

questions.explanation: wave means to move the hand from side to side.

questions.questionText: 'Hop like a rabbit' means we ___ .
questions.explanation: rabbits hop by jumping on one foot.

questions.questionText: Which word names a colour we often sing about in songs?
questions.explanation: red is a colour; run, sit and open are action words.

questions.questionText: In a chant, 'twist your body' means we ___ .

options.label: B
options.text: sit down on the chair quietly

options.label: D
options.text: turn our body from side to side

questions.explanation: twist means to turn the body from side to side.

questions.questionText: 'Nod your head' means we ___ .

options.label: B
options.text: move our head up and down

options.label: D
options.text: shake our head left and right

questions.explanation: nod means to move the head up and down.

questions.questionText: Which group has ONLY action words?
questions.explanation: clap, jump and stamp are all things we do.

questions.questionText: 'Turn around' in an action song means we ___ .

options.label: A
options.text: spin our body in a circle

questions.explanation: turn around means to spin in a circle.

questions.questionText: In the line 'Wash your hands and wash your face', which word tells us what we do with water?
questions.explanation: wash tells us the action we do with water.

questions.questionText: 'Blink your eyes' means we ___ .

options.label: C
options.text: open and close our eyes quickly

questions.explanation: blink means to open and close the eyes quickly.

questions.questionText: Which word rhymes with 'hand'?
questions.explanation: hand and stand end with the same sound /and/.

questions.questionText: In the line 'Stamp your feet upon the floor', what does 'upon' mean?
questions.explanation: upon means on top of something.

questions.questionText: Which pair are action words in a chant about animals?
questions.explanation: hop and jump are things we do; the others name animals, colours or numbers.

questions.questionText: Complete the rhyme: 'Clap your hands, one, two, three, / Clap your hands and smile at ___ .'
questions.explanation: three rhymes with me.

questions.questionText: Complete the rhyme: 'The sun is up, the sky is blue, / Little birds are singing ___ .'
questions.explanation: blue rhymes with too.

questions.questionText: Complete the rhyme: 'Touch your nose and touch your ear, / Touch your eyes from far to ___ .'
questions.explanation: ear rhymes with near.

questions.questionText: Complete the rhyme: 'Little bird up in the tree, / Sing your song so loud and ___ .'
questions.explanation: tree rhymes with free.

questions.questionText: Complete the rhyme: 'Wave your hand up in the sky, / Wave your hand and say ___ .'
questions.explanation: sky rhymes with goodbye.

questions.questionText: Complete the rhyme: 'Stamp your feet upon the floor, / Stamp your feet and shout for ___ .'
questions.explanation: floor rhymes with more.

questions.questionText: Complete the rhyme: 'Pitter, patter, raindrops fall, / On the window, on the ___ .'
questions.explanation: fall rhymes with wall.

questions.questionText: Complete the rhyme: 'Yellow banana, sweet and bright, / Eat it up with all your ___ .'
questions.explanation: bright rhymes with might.

questions.questionText: Complete the rhyme: 'The fish swims in the water blue, / It looks so happy, so do ___ .'
questions.explanation: blue rhymes with you.

questions.questionText: Complete the rhyme: 'I have a cat, her name is Dot, / She likes to sleep right on my ___ .'
questions.explanation: Dot rhymes with cot.

questions.questionText: Read the rhyme: 'Twist your body, turn around, / Touch the ground without a sound.' What do we do with our body?
questions.explanation: The first line tells us to twist and turn around.

questions.questionText: Read the rhyme: 'Wash your hands and wash your face, / Brush your teeth all over the place.' What is this rhyme about?
questions.explanation: Washing hands, face and brushing teeth are ways to keep clean.

questions.questionText: Read the rhyme: 'In the morning I wake up, / Comb my hair and have my cup.' What do we do after we wake up?
questions.explanation: The rhyme says we comb our hair after waking up.

questions.questionText: Read the rhyme: 'Clap, clap, stamp, stamp, / Jump up high and then we camp.' How many actions are in the first line?
questions.explanation: The first line has clap and stamp, two actions.

questions.questionText: Read the rhyme: 'The monkey climbs up very high, / And swings his tail toward the sky.' How does the monkey feel?
questions.explanation: A monkey climbing high and swinging its tail looks happy and free.

questions.questionText: Read the rhyme: 'Nod your head and blink your eye, / Wave to all as you pass by.' When we 'pass by', we are ___ .
questions.explanation: pass by means to walk past someone.

questions.questionText: Read the rhyme: 'Open your book and take your pen, / Write your name and start again.' Where are we, in this rhyme?
questions.explanation: Opening a book and writing with a pen happens in class.

questions.questionText: Read the rhyme: 'Hop, little rabbit, hop, hop, hop, / Stop, little rabbit, at the top.' Where does the rabbit stop?
questions.explanation: The rhyme says the rabbit stops at the top.

questions.questionText: Read the rhyme: 'Run, run, run to the gate, / Run, run, run, and do not wait.' Why does the runner 'do not wait'?

options.label: A
options.text: because the runner wants to keep running

options.label: C
options.text: because it is time to sleep

questions.explanation: The runner keeps running and does not stop or wait.

questions.questionText: Read the rhyme: 'Red and yellow, green and white, / Mix the colours, what a sight!' What can the speaker do?
questions.explanation: The line 'Mix the colours' tells us so.

questions.questionText: In an action song, the teacher sings 'Jump!'. What should we do?
questions.explanation: Jump means we jump up and down.

questions.questionText: The chant says 'Stand up!'. What do we do next?
questions.explanation: Stand up means to rise from a sitting position.

questions.questionText: If a rhyme says 'Good morning, teacher', when do we sing it?
questions.explanation: 'Good morning' is used in the morning.

questions.questionText: The action song says 'Touch your toes!'. Which part of the body do we touch?
questions.explanation: toes are on our feet.

questions.questionText: The rhyme says 'The sun is up'. What time of day is it?
questions.explanation: When the sun is up, it is daytime.

questions.questionText: If the song says 'Close the door', we should ___ .
questions.explanation: Close means shut.

questions.questionText: Read the rhyme: 'Two little birds sitting on a wall, / One named Peter, one named Paul.' How many birds are there?
questions.explanation: Two little birds: Peter and Paul.

questions.questionText: Read the rhyme: 'Stars up in the sky so bright, / Shining on us every night.' When do we see the stars?
questions.explanation: The rhyme says the stars shine every night.

questions.questionText: In a chant, the teacher says 'Now, stop!'. What should the pupils do?
questions.explanation: Stop means to stop moving at once.

questions.questionText: Read the rhyme: 'The bus goes beep, beep, beep, / Down the street, beep, beep, beep.' What makes the 'beep' sound?
questions.explanation: Buses beep with their horn.

questions.questionText: Read the rhyme: 'Milk in a glass, bread on a plate, / Eat your breakfast, don't be late.' Which meal is this rhyme about?
questions.explanation: The rhyme says 'Eat your breakfast'.

questions.questionText: The action song says 'Turn to your friend and smile!'. What should we do?

options.label: A
options.text: smile at the person beside us

questions.explanation: A friend in class is the person beside us.

questions.questionText: Read the rhyme: 'Raindrops tap on the window pane, / I love to listen to the rain.' How does the speaker feel about the rain?
questions.explanation: 'I love to listen' shows the speaker is happy.

questions.questionText: Read the rhyme: 'I put on my shoes and tie the lace, / Out I go to the open space.' Where is the speaker going?
questions.explanation: 'Out I go' means the speaker goes outside.

questions.questionText: Read the rhyme: 'The clock goes tick, tock, tick, tock, / It tells us when to eat and talk.' What does the clock help us know?
questions.explanation: A clock tells us the time.
